items.title: The Fourth Dimension of Science Diplomacy
items.evidence_note: Journal appears on the main Radar trusted-venue list; article-level peer review and claims require checking.
items.abstract_or_context: In a previous contribution, we highlighted how growing geopolitical tensions were beginning to challenge the principles of openness and international cooperation that have long characterised science.1 The increasing relevance of research security, trusted research, technology sovereignty and cooperation among like-minded countries has transformed the landscape of scientific cooperation. Consequently, the traditional openness of science can no longer be taken for granted.

This study examines how India's Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 and associated renewable energy policies influence renewable energy adoption in the commercial building sector. items.title: Vulnerabilities and agency of small technologically advanced states: Finland navigating Sino-US strategic technology competition
items.evidence_note: Journal appears on the main Radar trusted-venue list; article-level peer review and claims require checking.
items.abstract_or_context: This article explores how a small technologically advanced state, exemplified by Finland, seeks to maintain agency and manage security risks in Sino-US strategic technology competition, and what future options experts envision for it. The US and China are presently the only ‘geoeconomic great powers’ with competences across four dimensions: investment leverage, supply chains, critical technologies, and technology standards. Given its close security ties to the United States, Finland is expected to align with it when faced with a choice between technological ecosystems.
